facts.text: Sherrills Ford got its name from the ford Adam Sherrill crossed in 1747, marking the first European settlement west of the Catawba River.
The Neill–Turner–Lester House and the Miles Alexander Sherrill House in Sherrills Ford are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Mountain Creek Park spans 606 acres, offering biking, hiking, and trail‑running trails that wind through Sherrills Ford’s wooded hills.
A satellite office of the Catawba County Sheriff’s Department sits in Sherrills Ford, alongside the community library that preserves local history.
Sherrills Ford rests at an elevation of 204 meters (670 feet), placing it comfortably within the Piedmont’s rolling terrain.
The town lies along the northwestern shore of Lake Norman, giving residents easy access to one of North Carolina’s largest reservoirs.
